guidance.copy.macos_accessibility.title: ClipVault needs Accessibility permission
guidance.copy.macos_accessibility.summar: macOS must allow ClipVault to send keyboard events so it can press Cmd+V in the application you are typing into.
guidance.copy.macos_accessibility.step_3: Enable ClipVault (or the development build you are running).
guidance.copy.macos_accessibility.step_4: Return to ClipVault and select Retry.
guidance.copy.linux_x11_backend_unavaila: ClipVault could not reach the X11 paste backend
Synthetic paste needs a working X11 display and the XTEST extension. Check the session, display and sandbox permissions before retrying.
Confirm that ClipVault is running inside the graphical X11 session you want to paste into.
Confirm that $DISPLAY is set and the XTEST extension is enabled.
If ClipVault runs in Flatpak, Snap or another sandbox, enable the desktop integration permissions declared by the package.
Return to ClipVault and select Retry.
Wayland has no portable synthetic paste
ClipVault cannot inject keystrokes under Wayland without a compositor-specific portal. There is no universal setting for this; availability depends on the compositor.
Open history and copy entries with your usual keyboard shortcut if your compositor provides one.
For automatic paste, switch to an X11 session or configure a compositor-specific paste portal.
History, capture and search continue to work without synthetic paste.
guidance.copy.linux_unknown_session.titl: ClipVault could not identify a compatible graphical session
guidance.copy.linux_unknown_session.summ: ClipVault did not detect X11 or Wayland on this host. Synthetic paste is unavailable until a supported session is active.
guidance.copy.linux_unknown_session.step: Launch ClipVault from a graphical X11 or Wayland session.
Avoid running ClipVault over plain SSH without a forwarded display.
Select Retry after the graphical session is available.
guidance.copy.backend_unavailable.title: ClipVault could not complete the operation
guidance.copy.backend_unavailable.summar: The platform backend refused the request and ClipVault could not determine the cause. The history entry was not changed.
guidance.copy.backend_unavailable.step_2: If the issue persists, restart ClipVault and check the application logs.
guidance.copy.unknown.title: Unexpected platform failure
guidance.copy.unknown.summary: ClipVault encountered an unexpected platform failure. No clipboard content was sent to diagnostic output.
guidance.copy.unknown.step_2: If the failure continues, open ClipVault diagnostics and confirm the host platform.
guidance.copy.linux_settings_fallback.st: Confirm that you are running inside the graphical X11 session you intend to paste into.
Confirm that $DISPLAY is set and XTEST is enabled.
If you use a sandbox, enable the desktop integration permissions declared by the package.
Launch ClipVault from a graphical X11 or Wayland session.
Avoid running ClipVault over plain SSH without a forwarded display.
Select Retry after the graphical session is available.
Return to ClipVault and try the operation again.
Open the operating system settings manually.
Refer to ClipVault documentation for the relevant settings panel.

gnome.status.title: Integration status
gnome.status.activation_pending: The extension is installed in ~/.local/share/gnome-shell/extensions/, but GNOME Shell has not completed the connection. If you updated ClipVault, first select Reinstall extension to copy the current resource. Then sign out of GNOME and sign in again: in GNOME Shell 42, disabling and enabling an extension may not reload its already loaded module. After signing in, confirm that ClipVault is enabled under Extensions and start ClipVault again.

gnome.status.disconnected: The extension is installed, but the local connection was lost. The listener retries automatically. If the issue persists, open GNOME Extensions and confirm that clipvault@clipvault.app is enabled.
gnome.status.incompatible: This GNOME Shell version is not supported by the extension. ClipVault continues capturing with its other adapters.
